current_row.boundary_rationale: The book's opening word is אֵיכָ֣ה (oshb:Lam.1.1, byte tier), the verse-initial cry that gives this stretch its aleph line and frames a third-person report of the ruined capital: “How the city sits solitary, that was full of people! She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!” web:Lam.1.1. The same voice names the daughter-of-Zion formula at web:Lam.1.6 inside “All majesty has departed from the daughter of Zion.” web:Lam.1.6 (this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged by the present reading; the formula itself recurs seven further times book-wide, sweep: 8 verses book-wide), and keeps the same distance through the roads, gates and priests of web:Lam.1.4. The report closes on “She has no comforter.” web:Lam.1.9 immediately followed by the first-person plea “See, Yahweh, my affliction; for the enemy has magnified himself.” web:Lam.1.9, a brief intrusion of Zion's own voice inside an otherwise third-person span (a per-bytes deviation from a plain city_lament reading, disclosed rather than smoothed over). The same verse completes the contiguous refrain אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier; roughly "she is without a comforter"; sweep of the two-word refrain: 3 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), and refrains close units under the owner-ruled seam law: the boundary sits here rather than folding this verse forward with the interjection that follows it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The narrator's report continues past the refrain close, reporting the adversary's hand spread out on all her pleasant things and the nations who have entered her sanctuary: “concerning whom you commanded that they should not enter into your assembly.” web:Lam.1.10, where the second-person perfect צִוִּ֔יתָה and the second-person pronoun לָֽךְ (oshb:Lam.1.10, byte tier) address the deity directly, the same imperative-plus-vocative address that stands one verse behind the front seam at web:Lam.1.9. No first-person-singular form stands in this verse or the one that follows: “All her people sigh. They seek bread. They have given their pleasant things for food to refresh their soul.” web:Lam.1.11 (a ketiv/qere note also marks this verse per the inventory, not engaged by the present reading) keeps the same voice up to the point where its own close breaks into a second first-person plea, “Look, Yahweh, and see, for I have become despised.” web:Lam.1.11. This second interjection stands at a held edge this reading does not resolve: whether it, like the one before it, is a momentary breach inside the report or the true onset of Zion's own voice, which the next stretch takes up in full at web:Lam.1.12.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Zion's own prayer closes the poem: “Look, Yahweh, and see to whom you have done thus!” web:Lam.2.20, opening on the same petition imperative רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier) that already stood at oshb:Lam.1.11 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), then presses that plea through the horror of women eating their own children and priest and prophet slain in the sanctuary before turning to the day of slaughter itself: “You have called, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side.” web:Lam.2.22. The three-token form בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier; roughly "in the day of the anger of Yahweh") stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, this three-token form) and so closes the poem as a form attested once, not a repeating pattern; the shorter token it opens with, בְּי֥וֹם (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, this short token), is itself byte-identical to the token that opens the same wrath phrase at the poem's own aleph line, בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse book-wide, byte tier, this two-token phrase), so the poem's last verse closes an inclusio with its own first verse. The chapter's own PE mark closes web:Lam.2.22.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The dalet, he and vav triplets (3:10-12, 3:13-15, 3:16-18) continue the geber's first-person catalogue of affliction under the same voice as the triplets just before them. Lam.3.17 opens with a form capable of both a direct address to the deity and a statement about the speaker's own soul — וַתִּזְנַ֧ח (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier) beside נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Lam.3.17, byte tier) — and this span's same-voice warrant rests on the reading that keeps the third person across these verses. The unit ends on a line of declared exhaustion of hope, spliced at byte tier as אָבַ֣ד נִצְחִ֔י וְתוֹחַלְתִּ֖י מֵיְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.18, byte tier), rendered inside the WEB witness's own quotation as “My strength has perished, along with my expectation from Yahweh.” (web:Lam.3.18): a declared exhaustion of hope that sets up, but does not itself cross into, the imperative turn of the following verse.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this span through Lam.3.19-Lam.3.21 to include the zayin triplet was considered because the imperative onset זְכָר (oshb:Lam.3.19, byte tier) carries the same movement from despair to remembered hope that Lam.3.18’s declared exhaustion of hope anticipates; it was rejected because Lam.3.18’s declared exhaustion of hope offers a clearer seam for the vav triplet’s own close than the imperative onset of Lam.3.19 does.
